# Recipe — add an event

## 0. First, prove you want an event at all

| You want… | Use | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Something **done** | **Call the service.** | You get a return value, an error path, and compile-time checking. |
| To announce something that **already happened**, and you neither know nor care who reacts | **Publish a fact.** | Decoupling is the point. |

**An event is a past-tense fact, never a command** (rule #1). `ShowDialogEvent` and `PlaySfxEvent`
are banned: they are service calls that have thrown away every guarantee. Want a dialog shown? Call
`IDialogService`. Want a sound? Call `IAudioService`.

Name the type as a completed fact: `MatchEnded`, `CurrencyGranted`, `SceneChanged` — never
`ShowX`, `PlayX`, `DoX`.

**A new event type is a spine change** (`AGENTS.framework.md` §6) — route it.

## 1. Edit the manifest

`Tools/Codegen/Manifests/Events/game.events.json` — append one entry:

```json
{
  "name": "ShopPurchased",
  "order": 3,
  "summary": "A shop item was bought and its grants were applied.",
  "params": [
    { "name": "ItemId", "type": "string" },
    { "name": "Price",  "type": "long" }
  ]
}
```

Params become named, typed constructor parameters on a generated record. Each record implements
`WireName()` and `WriteParams(IEventParamWriter)`; providers consume those methods without reflection.
These are methods, so record text and the disk buffer's serialized properties remain unchanged.

Wire names and parameter keys use the shared `WireText.Snake` convention: `AdUnitId` → `ad_unit_id`,
`HTTPStatus` → `http_status`, `Level2Score` → `level2_score`, `TimeSeconds` → `time_seconds`, `ID` → `id`.
An event's `wireName` overrides its wire name; a param's `wireName` overrides its key. Wire names are
append-only: keep a shipped wire name when renaming a C# record by declaring the old `wireName`.

Codegen validates every event before writing any key, localization or event file:

- Names and keys match `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,39}$`; at most 25 params, with unique keys per event.
- Event wire names are unique across all framework and SKU event manifests.
- Firebase reserved event names (including `error`, `first_open`, `session_start`, `screen_view`,
  `ad_impression` and the complete list in `EventManifest`) are forbidden. The prefixes `firebase_`,
  `google_`, `ga_`, `fb_` are forbidden on both names and keys.
- Closed param types are `string`, `int`, `long`, `float`, `double`, `bool`. They must not declare
  `wire`. Every other type declares `"wire": "enum"` (snake_case of `value.ToString()`) or
  `"wire": "string"` (invariant text), for example `{ "name": "Source", "type": "GrantSource", "wire": "enum" }`.
- `int`/`long` write as `long`; `float`/`double` as `double`; bool stays bool; a null string is omitted.
  Providers needing narrower types use `WireValues.AsLong(bool)` and `WireValues.ToText(long|double|bool)`
  for invariant formatting (double round-trip `R`, bool `1`/`0`).

In consumers, the collision gate reads framework manifests from `--framework-manifests <dir>` when
provided, otherwise the repo package, the framework's `file:` dependency (relative to `Packages/`),
then exactly one matching `Library/PackageCache/com.classicspins.prototype-framework@*/CodegenManifests~`.
With SKU event manifests, an unreachable or ambiguous framework catalog exits 2 and lists probes.
The editor passes the package's `resolvedPath`; only this repo's package manifests are emitted.
No SKU event manifests means a missing framework catalog is a clean skip.

## 2. Generate

```
Framework/Codegen/Generate
```

`Assets/<Sku>/Gen/GameEvents.gen.cs` gains the record. **Never hand-edit a `.gen.cs` file.**

## 3. Register the broker — this step cannot be skipped

**MessagePipe has no source generator.** Every event type needs one explicit line, and that line
lives **only** in a file under `Installers/`:

```csharp
builder.RegisterMessageBroker<ShopPurchased>(new MessagePipeOptions());
```

A `RegisterMessageBroker<T>` anywhere outside `Installers/` **fails the CI grep by `file:line`**.
This is permanent boilerplate; no upstream relief is coming.

## 4. Publish and subscribe

Publish from the owner of the fact — the thing that made it true. Subscribe in whichever scope
cares; the subscription dies with that scope (`architecture-map.md` §2), so there is nothing to
unsubscribe manually.

**Gameplay never calls `IAnalytics` directly.** A forwarder maps the domain fact to a typed
analytics event. Keep that direction: fact in gameplay → forwarder → analytics.

## 5. Gate

```sh
Tools/Build/pf-build.sh codegen --check
sh Tools/CI/greps.sh source            # MessagePipe registration outside Installers/
```

## Framework facts already defined

`Runtime/Domain/Gen/GameEvents.gen.cs`: `CurrencyGranted` · `AdShown` · `AdRewarded` · `AdFailed` ·
`PurchaseSucceeded` · `PurchaseFailed` · `PurchaseRestored` · `SceneChanged` · `DialogOpened` ·
`DialogClosed` · `AdRevenuePaid`.

`AdRevenuePaid` differs from the rest of the catalog in its producer and its payload: it is tracked
only by an ads module's impl layer calling `IAnalytics.Track` (never mapped by the
`AnalyticsForwarder`, never registered as a MessagePipe broker), and it carries money — money is
counted only from it, never from `AdShown` / `AdRewarded`. Its parameters are append-only: the
analytics buffer rebinds by parameter name, so none is ever renamed, retyped, removed or reordered,
and a new one is appended at the end.

Domain facts published by framework services: `WalletChanged` · `ConsentChanged` · `SceneChange` ·
`DialogChange` · `AdVisibilityChanged` · `AdReadinessChanged` · `RemoteConfigFetched`. Subscribe to
these rather than inventing a parallel event.

`AdReadinessChanged(Placement, Ready)` is published by an ads module (never by the fake) and only on a
change. (1) Subscribe first, (2) then call `IsReadyAsync(p)` once; (3) no fact yet means *ask*, never
*not ready*; (4) `IBufferedSubscriber<AdReadinessChanged>` is a defect (it replays a `default`); (5)
offer only while the latest `Ready` ∧ `IAdGate.CanShow(p)` —
`An_offer_is_hidden_for_a_remove_ads_owner_on_an_interstitial_placement_even_when_ready`.

## Common failures

| Symptom | Cause |
|---|---|
| Nothing receives the publish | No `RegisterMessageBroker<T>` for that type. |
| CI names a `file:line` for MessagePipe | The registration is outside `Installers/`. Move it. |
| Review rejects the event | The name is imperative — it is a command, not a fact. |
| A subscription outlives its screen | It was taken in the wrong scope. Subscribe in the scope that should own it. |
